name: Real-word error: a valid word, and the wrong one
name_fr: Faute en mot valide : un mot du dictionnaire, et le mauvais

origin.campaign: Deep Statistical Analysis of OCR Errors for Effective Post-OCR Processing, JCDL 2019

seen.corpus: historical newspapers and books, OCR output analysed against ground truth
seen.document: 'hear' read as 'bear' — valid in the dictionary, wrong in context
seen.excerpt: Real-word errors are valid in dictionary but incorrect in context (e.g. 'hear' vs. 'bear'). […] non-word errors are invalid in dictionary (e.g. 'hear' vs. 'hcar'). It is obvious that non-word errors are easier to be detected and corrected than real-word errors. — Measured: real-word errors account for about 59.21 % of OCR errors.

prevention.note: no dictionary sees it; only the context does, and that is not a deterministic check

repair.note: the value is wrong, not extra: deleting removes a true fact rather than correcting the word

proposed_severity.reason: It passes every lexical check because it is a word. Nothing signals it: the sentence reads, the value looks sound, and the fact drawn from it is false. And it is the majority case at 59.21 %, not the margin — which reverses the risk profile a catalogue of visible OCR confusions leaves a reader with.
proposed_severity.reason_fr: Elle passe tout contrôle lexical, puisque c'est un mot. Rien ne la signale : la phrase se lit, la valeur a l'air saine, et le fait qu'on en tire est faux. Et c'est le cas majoritaire à 59,21 %, pas la marge — ce qui renverse le profil de risque que laisse croire un catalogue de confusions OCR visibles.
proposed_severity.proposed_by: Claude Banc à vérité connue (LLM agent)
